subject: Post-demo intake: model recommendations, prompt samples & redaction guidance
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@legaltech.ai>, Samuel Diaz <sam.diaz@legaltech.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo intake: model recommendations, prompt samples & redaction guidance

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciated the clear use-case context on clause extraction + inferred risk flags. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Short recap: You want a high-precision extractor for legal contracts (clauses, parties, effective dates) plus a parallel quality signal for risky language. Latency target is ~150–300ms per document in a batched worker; throughput estimate ~50–200 docs/min depending on batch.

- Preliminary model fit (what we showed / recommend):
  * Llama 2.1 Chat 13B (q4f16) — best balance of fidelity and cost for high-precision extraction workloads.
  * Mistral-Instruct 7B — strong for classification/regression-style quality signals and lower cost for high throughput.
  * Redwood safety-tuned 30B variant (for customers wanting the highest recall across edge legal phrasing) — we typically use this as a canary/fallback when precision drops.

- Evaluation artifacts we can share: a short benchmark we ran on a 2k-document simulated contract corpus (link below), plus our recommended prompt skeletons for extraction + risk scoring.

What I need from you to make the evaluation concrete:
1) A seed set of 50–100 representative contract prompts/samples that cover the clause formats you care about (we'll use these for a quick precision/recall sweep). If possible include some of the edge cases you mentioned in the call (handwritten amendments, mixed-language snippets, redacted fields).
2) A list of fields you want extracted (canonical names) and any tolerance/priority (e.g., "party name" = high precision, "implied termination reason" = high recall).
3) Any parts of the documents that must be redacted before sending to Redwood (PII/SSN/client IDs). If redaction is required we can accept samples with placeholders and will provide a redaction checklist.

Attachments: post-demo-screenshots.png (screens from the model profiler), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft timeline + milestones).

I also dropped two quick links below: our public benchmark preview and the HubSpot deal so you have context.

Links: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/preview/2027-02-search-eval  |  https://hubspot.redwood.ai/deal/DL-2027-0198

Proposed next steps: If you can share the seed prompt set and a short priority list by EOD Wednesday (3/17) we’ll run a 72-hour mini-eval and return a short report with recommended model and quantization profile for your throughput/latency targets.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap and the demo was very clear. A few clarifying points from our side: 

- We can assemble a 75-sample seed set by Wednesday EOD; these will be redacted to replace client names with CLIENT_X and will include 8 documents with handwritten amendments. Is that OK for the mini-eval?
- Priority fields: party_name (high precision), effective_date (high precision), notice_period (medium), implied_term_violations (high recall) — I’ll put these in the seed manifest.
- Security: we prefer to send redacted samples for the first pass. Can you confirm what level of redaction you require (full redaction vs token masking)? Also please send any required contact for the security questionnaire — I see a placeholder on your website.

I attached a very small sample prompt file so you can see our (rough) internal formatting. Also attached our initial internal security questionnaire (we usually share this with vendors early).

Attaching: legaltech_sample_prompts.txt (text/plain), security-questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)

If you can confirm redaction guidance and whether the 75-sample seed (redacted) works for the 72-hour mini-eval, we’ll aim to deliver on Wednesday.

Thanks,

Nora / Marissa / Ben — following up with the technical intake and a redaction checklist that should make it easy for LegalTech to prepare the seed set without us handling raw PII.

Action items we will execute once we receive the redacted seed set and manifest:
1) 72-hour mini-eval across the three recommended variants (Llama2-chat-13B q4, Mistral-Instruct-7B, Redwood safety-30B). We'll return precision/recall at field level + latency P95 numbers.
2) If you require, we can run the same tests on a Dedicated pool (we'll include a separate cost line).
3) Deliverable: short PDF with model recommendation, quantization suggestion, and a suggested rollout canary (traffic split + fallback).

Redaction checklist (attached): token placeholder for personal names (CLIENT_X), replace SSNs with <REDACTED_SSN>, mask email addresses to user@domain.tld -> user@REDACTED, and include a manifest.csv describing which fields were redacted and why. If anything is regulatory-sensitive we can sign an addendum and route to our Private deployment onboarding.

Attachments: redaction-checklist.pdf (application/pdf), eval-benchmarks-20270210.csv (text/csv)

I’ll also upload the short benchmark snapshot to the preview link Marissa included so you can see the scoring matrix. If you want a quick sync to walk through the checklist, I’m free tomorrow morning.
